A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Star Attention work. All 18 pages of v2 and 16 pages of v3, including Appendices A–D, support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark accuracies, inference timings and anchor-block ablations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark, timing and ablation results, including Tables 1–6 and the task-category results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The anchor-based context encoding and distributed global query/decoding procedures are unchanged. Appendix A removes explanatory comments and combines token-generation statements without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 13 RULER tasks, five BABILong tasks and the same ten-task InfiniteBench comparison in Table 3. Evaluated domains and languages are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Ring/full attention, StreamingLLM, MInference and vanilla autoregressive generation. Table 3 shortens 'MInference 1.0' to 'MInference' while retaining its scores; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Models, prompts, sample counts and sequence/block settings match. Table 4's revised differences often correspond to relative rather than absolute percentage-point losses, but its caption still specifies absolute degradation and several entries fit neither calculation. Whether this represents a metric revision or numerical reporting errors is unresolved.

E4.justification: The anchor-position, content and size ablation configurations and underlying accuracies remain unchanged. The attention-sink illustration, accuracy–speed analysis and Appendix D task-category analyses are retained without new analytical questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The tables and performance plots retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 4 retains all raw accuracies but revises both difference columns. At 128K, random-token anchors change from −15.86% to −10.15%, and first-block-content anchors from −3.55% to −0.96%, despite unchanged scores. Other benchmark results and performance plots are retained.

T1.justification: The block definitions, distributed-softmax Equations (1)–(4) and Appendix A aggregation expressions are unchanged. No mathematical definition, assumption or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same two-phase contribution, compatibility without fine-tuning, and claim of up to 11× speedup while preserving 97–100% of baseline accuracy.

C2.justification: The attention-sink explanation, unresolved anchor-size mechanism, multi-hop limitations and aggregation interpretation remain unchanged. The new generic Impact Statement introduces no specific scientific limitation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 explicitly states that anchor and context block sizes match in all speedup experiments and clarifies Table 7's scope. This adds documentation rather than establishing a changed setting; hardware counts, precision, prompt templates and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces Srebro and Jaakkola's Weighted Low-Rank Approximations (2003) with Hu et al.'s LoRA (2022), with corresponding reference-list changes. The broader research positioning is retained; other reference edits mainly concern bibliographic presentation.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. v3 adds an Impact Statement, expands acknowledgements, shortens pseudocode comments and makes limited caption, terminology and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: v3 converts the main text to a two-column conference layout and extensively reflows figures and tables. Figure 3 gains standardized axes and sink/anchor annotations. The panels of v2 Figure 6 become separate Figures 6 and 7, while the appendix plot becomes Figure 8.

improvement.justification: Clearer Figure 3 annotations and the Appendix B.2 clarification provide limited benefits, but Table 4 introduces numerical inconsistencies. Its retained 98.49 and 82.63 accuracies imply a 15.86-point drop, correctly reported in v2; v3 instead reports 10.15%. Similar new mismatches weaken the reliability of the ablation reporting and outweigh the modest presentation and documentation gains.
